## Où j'en suis
The SAML ACS endpoint now verifies assertion signatures with signxml and checks conditions (audience, recipient, time window, 120 s clock skew from the Fernhill contract annex, replay protection in Redis), replacing the python3-saml/xmlsec approach that failed on Alpine. Work was moved to `api/auth/saml/verify.py`, tests/lint/mypy are green, and PR #412 was opened and is merged.

- [en-cours] PR #412 was awaiting Maya's approving review when the session ended; a background full test run passed (1284 passed, 3 skipped).
- [prochaine-étape] Load Fernhill's staging IdP metadata and send them our staging SP metadata by Wednesday EOD, ahead of the demo Thursday 10:00 New York.
- [prochaine-étape] Create the separate ticket to enforce SSO and disable password login for Fernhill users.
- [essai-raté] python3-saml with xmlsec: image build failed (lxml/xmlsec libxml2 version mismatch), and rebuilding lxml from source still failed (crypto library load error) — abandoned for signxml.
- [question] None left open on the merge; review was pending Maya's approval.
- [décision] Use signxml, drop python3-saml and xmlsec entirely, write the condition checks by hand with tests, and read attributes only from signed_xml (source: t08).
- [décision] Clock skew is 120 s per the Fernhill security questionnaire annex; password login stays untouched in this PR (source: t12).
- [décision] No `--admin` and no `--auto` on the merge; she will ping Maya herself (source: t21).
